logo.title: The Crown & Pint.
logo.lead: A crown sitting on a full pint: the Queen's Head, and the Queen Mother's famous pint, in one mark. It's gold on oxblood like a Victorian gilded pub sign, and it works on a beer mat, a chalkboard or a hanging sign. The wordmark is set in Abril Fatface, the heavy display type of old signwriting.

story.title: Saved by locals, for locals.
story.lead: The Queen's Head has stood on Flamborough Street since 1827. It's Grade II listed, believed to have inspired the Queen Vic, and the Queen Mother once famously pulled a pint here. In December 2023 a group of locals reopened it as a free house at community prices. The brand should feel like the best version of a proper East End boozer: gilded, warm, a bit cheeky and completely unpretentious.
story.positioning: The historic East End pub the neighbourhood saved. Real heritage, community prices, no pretension.

colour.title: Oxblood, gold leaf, bar tile.
colour.lead: Oxblood and gold leaf come straight from Victorian pub signs and etched mirrors. Bottle-green tile is the classic East End pub frontage. Cream is the nicotine-free ceiling we all remember as nicotine yellow.

type.title: Signwriter's display, honest sans.
type.lead: Abril Fatface has the fat, high-contrast look of hand-painted pub signs and chalkboards. Karla is plain and friendly for the menu, prices and quiz dates. Both are free on Google Fonts.

voice.title: Like the landlord at the bar.
voice.lead: Warm, funny and to the point. Be proud of the history without being precious about it. Always make it clear everyone is welcome. Never trade on the royal family in a way that implies endorsement.
pairs: "The Queen Mother pulled a pint here. You can too, if you're buying."
"By Royal Appointment." (We're not, and it's a protected phrase.)

imagery.title: Pints, faces, the bar.
imagery.lead: Warm, grainy photos of regulars (with permission), the bar and the tiles, quiz night mid-laugh, and the pub from the street at dusk. Archive photos of the Queen Mother's visit if the rights can be cleared. No stock beer splashes.
